topic: This week in AI: Anthropic files to go public, Microsoft buyouts, Google's ads exception, AI agent logins, 1 in 11 jobs
post:
An AI lab filed to go public, and a tech giant offered a quarter of its staff a way out. 📊
Here are this week's 5 AI stories worth your time, in 60 seconds.

1️⃣ Anthropic files for an IPO
The Claude maker filed its S-1 and plans to list on Nasdaq as "ANT". Reported first-half revenue: about $16.3 billion.

2️⃣ Microsoft offers buyouts
About 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of its workforce, were offered a voluntary exit as AI spending climbs.

3️⃣ Google's new ads exception
Its privacy policy now lets Gmail, Drive and Photos data you connect to its AI features help shape your ads.

4️⃣ AI agents log in, passwords stay hidden
1Password for Agents lets supported AI agents sign in for you, after you approve, without ever seeing the password.

5️⃣ 1 in 11 jobs
Goldman Sachs projects AI could displace about 9% of US workers over a decade, with big cuts likely waiting for a recession.

Why it matters:
This week was about money and trust: who pays for AI, who it replaces, and who gets your data. 🔍

Practical takeaway:
Pick one story and ask: what does this change for me on Monday? Then do one small thing about it. 🧠

Which story surprised you most? 👇

Follow for daily AI news you can actually use.
